content:
By Michelle Anderson · Mom + Blog Mama
Mom of two big kids and one snuggly farm dog. I write about real farm life, the recipes I actually cook on weeknights, and the little things that make our homestead feel like home.

Our Honest Review of the Cisily Sink Caddy Sponge Holder for Farmhouse Kitchens

First Impressions

I was juggling a mountain of dishes after the boys' soccer game on Thursday night, and Biscuit decided it was the perfect time to jump onto the counter for a snack. In the chaos, I caught a glimpse of the little stainless‑steel caddy sitting on our worn butcher‑block, looking like it belonged in a country‑style magazine. Honestly, I wasn't expecting a $11.69 kitchen gadget to make much of a splash, but it already felt like a tiny piece of order in the madness. The brush holder and the self‑draining tray seemed clever, and I was curious enough to give it a real quick spin.

→ See Cisily Sink Caddy Sponge Holder for Kitchen with Brush Holder and Stainless Steel Self Drain Tray, R on Amazon

Putting It to the Test

The first thing I did was fill the sponge compartment with our trusty dish‑spongy that the kids keep calling “the green monster.” I slipped the brush in the side slot, and the whole thing sat pretty much flat against the sink edge. When I turned the faucet on, the water dripped into the stainless steel tray and slid right down the little slope no standing water, no soggy mess. The boys were watching from the kitchen island, and I swear one of them whispered, “Mom, that’s fancy!” And that’s the kind of little win that makes a hectic evening feel a bit smoother.

I’ve had a few other caddies over the years some plastic, some ceramic so I could tell right away that the Cisily feels sturdier. The metal feels like it could survive a tumble if the dog decides to investigate, which is reassuring because Biscuit has a habit of nudging anything that looks like a new toy. I also liked the fact that the holder doesn’t cling to the side of the sink; it just rests there, which means it’s easy to lift out for a quick clean. The only thing that threw me off a bit was the size; it’s a tad wider than my old plastic one, so I had to shift the cutting board a couple of inches to make room. But honestly, that’s a small price to pay for the sleek look.

What Surprised Me

The funny thing is, after a week of using the Cisily, I actually started to notice the little things it helped with. The self‑draining tray keeps the sponge from turning into a swampy mess, which means fewer funky smells in the kitchen. My husband, who usually complains about “that damp sponge thing,” hasn’t mentioned it once since we started using this holder. And the brush slot? It actually keeps the scrubbing brush from getting lost under the faucet, which used to happen all the time when the kids were doing art projects and the brush would disappear. I even caught myself reaching for the brush without thinking about where it was talk about a subtle win.

Another pleasant surprise was the way the stainless steel catches the light. Our farmhouse kitchen has a lot of natural light pouring in through the big windows, and the caddy adds a tiny reflective sparkle that feels almost like a decorative piece rather than a functional one. I’ve found myself pausing for a second while I’m washing veggies, just to admire how the metal glints in the morning sun. It’s a small thing, but it adds a touch of charm that fits right in with our reclaimed wood cabinets and the old farmhouse sink.

A Tiny Drawback

Now, I’m not one to sugarcoat everything, so here’s the one thing that made me raise an eyebrow. The silicone base that’s supposed to keep the caddy from sliding around is a little softer than I expected. When you push the caddy to the side of the sink, it can shift a bit if you’re not careful, especially when the sink is full of suds. It’s not a deal‑breaker, but if you have a really busy kitchen with a lot of movement, you might find yourself nudging it back into place more often than you’d like. A little extra grip would’ve been nice, but at $11.69 it’s still a pretty good value.

Who Will Love It

If you’re anything like me someone who runs a household with three kids, a dog that thinks the kitchen is his personal playground, and a schedule that feels like a non‑stop marathon this little caddy could be a lifesaver. It’s perfect for anyone who loves that farmhouse aesthetic but doesn’t want to sacrifice practicality. The stainless steel design blends in with copper pots, wooden cutting boards, and the occasional vintage sign you might have hanging on the wall. And if you’re on a budget (who isn’t?), the price is honestly hard to beat for something that looks this polished and works this well.

I’ve already recommended it to a few of my mom friends during our weekly coffee catch‑ups, and they’ve all been eager to try it out. One of them even said she’d put it on her “must‑have kitchen gadgets” list after I showed her how the self‑draining tray works. So if you’re looking for a small upgrade that won’t break the bank and will actually make your sink area feel a little less chaotic, give the Cisily Sink Caddy a whirl.

→ Shop Cast Iron Cookware on Amazon

A Little Tip for New Owners

Okay, so here’s a quick tip before you place your order. When you first set it up, give the tray a quick rinse and let it dry completely before you start loading sponges and brushes. That little step helps the silicone base settle into its groove and reduces any initial slipping. Also, if you have a dishwasher, the caddy is safe to toss in there, but I’d still give it a hand‑wash every now and then to keep that shine looking fresh. The metal can get a bit of water spotting if you let it sit too long, and a little vinegar‑water wipe does the trick.

All in all, the Cisily Sink Caddy Sponge Holder for Kitchen has earned a permanent spot on our butcher‑block. It’s not a revolutionary invention, but it’s a solid, thoughtful piece that makes everyday chores a touch easier. And in a farmhouse kitchen where the vibe is all about warmth and simplicity, that’s exactly what we need. If you’re ready to ditch the soggy sponge pile and bring a little farmhouse flair to your sink, this caddy might just be the perfect fit.

content:
By Michelle Anderson · Mom + Blog Mama
Mom of two big kids and one snuggly farm dog. I write about real farm life, the recipes I actually cook on weeknights, and the little things that make our homestead feel like home.

Our Honest Review of the Wake In Cloud, Floral Comforter

First Night on the New Bed

When I finally got the kids to sleep in their own rooms (the boys finally stopped stealing my blankets at 2 a.m.), I decided it was time to give our little cottage bedroom a proper makeover. I pulled out the old floral quilt that had seen better days, dusted off the iron bed frame, and rolled out the Wake In Cloud, Floral Comforter Set. The moment I spread it over the mattress, the room felt like a scene from a storybook, and Biscuit the golden retriever immediately hopped up for a nap on the foot of the bed. The kids Mia, 7, and Eli, 5 were already giggling, calling it “the cloud you can jump on.”

I was honestly surprised by how soft the fabric felt; it’s not the cheap polyester you get on most budget sets. The stitching is tight enough that it didn’t start fraying after a couple of washes, and the vintage flower pattern actually looks like it was hand‑painted. I love that the colors are muted pastel pinks and creams, which blend perfectly with the lace curtains we hung last spring. The funny thing is, even the old wooden dresser we rescued from the attic seemed to smile a little.

→ See Wake In Cloud - Floral Comforter Set, Cute Vintage Flower Cottagecore Aesthetic for Women Teen Girls on Amazon

How It Fits Into Our Cottagecore Vibe

Our bedroom has always been a little homage to cottage life think reclaimed wood, a small vase of wildflowers, and a tea kettle that still whistles on the stove. Adding the Wake In Cloud set just amplified that vibe without feeling over‑the‑top. The comforter’s light weight makes it perfect for those warm summer nights when we leave the windows open and listen to crickets, yet it still gives enough warmth for a chilly fall evening when the kids are snuggled up reading bedtime stories.

I tried pairing it with a simple white throw and a few mismatched pillows we collected from thrift stores, and the whole look felt curated rather than forced. The floral print doesn’t clash with our pastel wall paint; instead, it ties everything together like a gentle, breezy chorus. And because it’s a set, the pillow shams match the comforter, which saves me the hassle of hunting down coordinating pieces at Target.

→ Shop Home Organization on Amazon

The Good, the Great, and the Tiny Nitpick

Honestly, the price point of $39.99 is a steal for a set that looks this polished. I’ve spent twice that on a “designer” comforter that turned out to be stiff and smelled like chemicals. The Wake In Cloud set washes well just a gentle cycle and tumble dry low, and it comes out fluffy without any hard clumps. The only thing I’d point out is that the comforter is a smidge thinner than I expected for the price. If you’re someone who loves to burrow deep into a heavy duvet on winter nights, you might want an extra blanket on top.

But for our cottagecore aesthetic, that lightness is actually a plus. It drapes nicely over the iron bed, creating that relaxed, “just rolled out of a meadow” look. The small detail that surprised me was the hidden pocket inside the comforter where you can tuck a small pillow or a favorite bedtime book. It’s a clever touch that we didn’t notice until we were packing the kids’ bedtime routine.

→ Shop Farmhouse Kitchen Essentials on Amazon

Real‑World Use: From Sunday Mornings to Soccer Practice

Sunday mornings are our “slow down” time pancakes, fresh coffee, and the kids drawing on the floor with crayons. The Wake In Cloud set makes those mornings feel extra cozy; the kids love to crawl out of bed and flop onto the soft comforter while I sip my coffee and watch Biscuit chase his tail. Then comes the hectic weekday rush: I’m juggling a quick school run, loading the car with soccer gear, and trying not to spill my latte on the new set. So far, no spills, no stains just a little bit of morning light dusting that a quick shake does the trick.

When Eli’s soccer practice ends late and he’s still buzzing with energy, we pull the kids onto the bed for a quick story session. The comforter’s breathable feel means they don’t overheat, and the floral design keeps the room feeling fresh even when the house is buzzing with activity. My husband, Jake, even admitted he’s tempted to swap his office chair for a spot on the bed just to enjoy the vibe.

Who Should Grab This One?

If you’re anything like me loving the cottagecore aesthetic but not wanting to break the bank this comforter set is right up your alley. It’s perfect for small spaces, especially those iron or vintage frames that need a little lift. The kids will adore the playful floral pattern, and the adults will appreciate the understated elegance.

Honestly, if you’re looking for a piece that ties together a cozy, lived‑in feel without the hassle of high‑maintenance fabrics, go for the Wake In Cloud, Floral Comforter Set. It won’t turn your bedroom into a hotel suite, but it will make it feel like a well‑kept country cottage that you can retreat to after a long day of farm chores or school runs.

And if you’re still on the fence, just remember that at $39.99 you’re getting a set that looks a lot pricier, feels soft, and adds that perfect touch of vintage charm we all crave.
